findings.where: First screen, top nav: 'Profile', 'Articles and talks' and 'Blog' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The three nav items have different labels but all go to the same place, the article specimen (#article). 'Profile' lands on a blog post about PPP law, not on anything about Mark, and 'Articles and talks' and 'Blog' can't be told apart by where they lead.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer checking who Mark is would click 'Profile' first. They land in the middle of an article and have to scroll around to find his background, which is the reason they opened the nav. The founder, clicking through the hero they judge first, hits the same dead end.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge' with its download arrow and 'PDF'
findings.fault: The row promises a PDF download (an arrow icon and the word 'PDF'), but the link goes to #article, the same page. Nothing downloads. Also, only the small blue 'PDF' looks clickable: the title is in grey reading ink, so the whole-row target looks static over most of its area, which goes against the page's own rule that blue marks what can be clicked.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants Mark's lecture to pass round their team clicks the PDF and gets nothing. The research and brief call the PDF list 'the product', and here its one specimen is a dead action.

findings.where: First screen header: the name 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra mark (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The lockup is split. The mark is a link home, but the name next to it, set off by a divider and treated as part of the same lockup, is static. A visitor expects the name-and-logo in the corner to act as one home link, and half of it does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who has scrolled into the article and taps the name at the top to get back gets no response. It's minor because the mark beside it works, but it is a hidden inconsistency on the part the brief puts first.

findings.where: Article specimen, the numbers of the three-item list
findings.fault: The list numbers are set in the house blue, which the page reserves for links and states as its rule ('Grey for reading, blue only where something can be clicked'). Static numbers borrow the link colour.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, adding articles, and readers who learn the page's blue-means-clickable rule: the numbers weaken the signal that blue is a link. Few would actually try to click a number.

findings.fault: This is a button that acts in place (it replays the animation), but it is dressed as a link: blue, underlined, with no edge or fill. It borrows navigation's reserved signifier, so it suggests the visitor will be taken somewhere.
findings.who_objects: The founder or Mark testing the motion sketch may expect it to jump to the top or open something, not play the animation in the preview frame. A small surprise on a low-stakes control.
